messages:
maria: heads up — ACME (prod) pinged support about p99 jump from APAC clients starting ~03:12 UTC. They report interactive latency spiking to ~2.5–3s. I collected traces and a quick traceroute, looks like requests are getting routed into us-west-2 unexpectedly. attaching snippets below.

Ajay: thanks. do we have a trace id or span ids? any change around 02:50–03:10?

maria: trace id 5f7b9a02-prod-ctx. Span timeline shows client -> edge-ap-sg -> egress-proxy-usw2 -> backend-usw2 -> model.

trace-bot: new trace 5f7b9a02-prod-ctx captured (jaeger link: https://jaeger.redwood/trace/5f7b9a02)

maria: traceroute from customer endpoint (ap-southeast-1):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (54.231.12.34), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.0.1  1.0 ms  0.9 ms  1.1 ms
 2  edge-ap-sg-01.redwood  12.3 ms  11.8 ms  12.0 ms
 3  transit-peer-asia  20.9 ms  21.0 ms  20.7 ms
 4  usw2-peering-node  120.4 ms  119.9 ms  121.0 ms
 5  model-backend-usw2  121.3 ms  120.8 ms  121.7 ms
```

maria: note hop 4 leaps to us-west-2 instead of local backbone to apac compute.

Sarah L.: interesting — only p99? are p50/p95 stable?

maria: p50/p95 fine. p99 elevated for token streaming responses only. no auth failures.

Ajay: could be recent egress routing change or peering cost-based routing. Kai, any recent rollout to routing-policy or egress-cost-preferences?

Kai: I pushed a small canary for the egress cost-policy at 02:52 UTC (3% of traffic) to prefer lower-cost inter-region peering. Noted it touched the egress selection code path that chooses region based on estimated egress cost + headroom.

Ajay: that matches timing. canary might be selecting cheaper US peering for some APAC prefixes — causing cross-region hop.

maria: repro steps I used from an APAC client: 
1) curl -v -H 'X-Client-Region: ap-southeast-1' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream\2) check response headers

Example output header I saw: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: redwood-edge
X-Edge-Region: ap-southeast-1
X-Egress-Region: us-west-2
X-Model-Server: model-xyz-usw2
```

maria: so edge is correct but egress chosen is us-west-2. that explains extra RTT.

Kai: I'm going to rollback the canary to 0% immediately. will report when done.

ops-bot: rollback action initiated by Kai — egress-cost-policy canary -> 0% (run id: rb-2026-2812).

Kai: rollback completed at 03:26 UTC. monitoring p99 now.

maria: after rollback, ACME reports p99 back to normal ~350ms within ~4 minutes. I also re-ran traceroute, now path stays in APAC.

Ajay: great. we should create an incident ticket and include: traces, traceroutes, canary config diff, and the curl repro. Also need to alert networking about peering-cost heuristic — it may be too aggressive for latency-sensitive customers.

Sarah L.: agreed. action items:
- maria: attach full jaeger trace and traceroute outputs to support ticket (#INC-2026-4321).
- Kai: postmortem on policy logic + add region-affinity override for high-priority tenants.
- Ajay: add an automated canary watch that compares egress-region vs edge-region for p99 alarms.

maria: opening ticket now with timestamps, trace link, and repro steps. tagging @networking and @infra.

maria: quick note for support playbook: if customer sees p99-only latency and edge-region != egress-region, check canary rollouts for egress routing and rollback. also include repro curl with X-Client-Region header.

trace-bot: incident INC-2026-4321 created, investigator assigned: Kai.

Kai: follow-up — adding a guard to prevent egress-cost-policy from choosing cross-continent egress for tenants with region-affinity metadata set. will PR today.

maria: thanks all. ACME confirmed degraded UX is resolved. closing loop with them and leaving incident open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
